course_summary:
ISEN 625 | Simulation Methods and Applications | Fall 2025
Instructor: Richard M. Feldman | richf@tamu.edu
Meets: Monday, Wednesday, 8:00 AM - 8:50 AM; Thursday, 8:00 AM - 10:30 AM | 1027 ETB
Grading: For students opting out of final: Lab test [24%], Lecture test [20%], Homework, labs, and attendance quizzes [12%]. For students taking final: Lab test [19.2%], Lecture test [16%], Homework, labs, and attendance quizzes [9.6%], Final exam [20%]. A: 90-100%, B: 80-89.9%, C: 70-79.9%, D: 60-69.9%, F: less than 60%.
Topics: linear congruential generator, multiplicative LCG, combined generators, entity dependent service times, pull systems (CONWIP), correlated normal variates, gamma random variates, Goodness-of-Fit Tests, K-S Test, Output Statistics, State Statistics, Tallies, Combiner/Separator, Q-Q Plots, Simio Processes, Stations, Non-stationary Poisson processes, estimating mean rates, Conveyors, Vehicles, Task sequences, changeover times, use of material, inventory ordering policies, Balking, reneging, queueing analysis, entity colors, status labels, experiment, properties, states, responses, time plots, random numbers, priorities, branching, random variate generation, distributions, statistics, finite buffers, random number streams, unequal servers in parallel, node lists, system cost, Sequences, Time varying arrival rates, schedules, comparing alternatives, Verification, validation, debugging techniques, discrete event (process-oriented) simulation modeling, simulation data preparation, analysis of simulation output, simulation modeling, commercial simulation language
Tools: Simio, Excel, Python, Canvas, Zoom, w3schools.com, anaconda.com
Prerequisites: STAT 212 or STAT 601
